question: How a maskedShieldType sprite (a country's flag cut to a shield, with its overlay) is loaded and drawn through gfx/FX/maskedflag.fx: the class, its keys, the effect, the technique, every parameter, the vertices, the states, and where the flag texture comes from.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::CMaskedSpriteType
addresses.signature: CMaskedSpriteType* __stdcall CMaskedSpriteType::CMaskedSpriteType(CMaskedSpriteType* this@stack:4, void* flagAtlas@stack:8, CGraphics* graphics@ECX) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Makes a `maskedShieldType`** (0x250 bytes, operator new at VA 0x8409CB in the spriteTypes factory 0x8408E0, which hands it ECX = the graphics and the flag atlas `&graphics +0x6BD6C`). Calls the CSpriteType constructor (VA 0xAB7450) with the graphics, writes the vftable (rva 0x11E1D44), stores the graphics at +0x1A0, empties the three strings +0x1A4 (textureFile2), +0x1C0 (textureFile1) and +0x1F4 (effectFile), sets both texture indices +0x210 and +0x214 to -1 and **stores the flag atlas at +0x244**. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84BE10..0x84BEC9: `mov edi, ecx` then `[esi+0x1a0] = edi`, vftable 0x15E1D44 written at 0x84BE47, three 0x40A160 string inits at +0x1A4/+0x1C0/+0x1F4, `or eax,-1` into +0x210/+0x214, `[ebp+0xc]` into +0x244, `ret 8`. findRefs --vftable CMaskedSpriteType finds this store and no other constructor; one caller at 0x8409F4 with `lea ecx,[edi+0x6bd6c]; push ecx; push eax(new 0x250); mov ecx, edi`. Wrong if the caller's EDI is not the graphics (CEU3Graphics::CEU3Graphics writes +0x6BD6C, so it is).

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::DeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 0: CMaskedSpriteType::~CMaskedSpriteType (rva 0x44BF00), then frees the object where bit 0 of `flags` is set. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84BED0..0x84BEEF: push esi; call 0x84BF00; test byte [ebp+8],1; call 0xB95F9B (free) on the object; ret 4. vtable.py --holding: CMaskedSpriteType slot 0 only.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::~CMaskedSpriteType
addresses.comment: Writes the vftable back, releases and frees the plain quad at +0x220 (its +4 object's slot 2, then free), hands the two texture indices +0x210 and +0x214 back to the texture handler (VA 0xA610E0, the handler `graphics +0x158` in EDI) where they are not negative, destroys the strings +0x1F4, +0x1C0 and +0x1A4, and calls the CSpriteType destructor (VA 0xAB7F60). `this` is the stack argument. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84BF00..0x84C010, read whole; the only caller is slot 0 (0x84BED7, `push esi; call`). Wrong if 0xA610E0 is not a release - it is called only where the index is >= 0 and with the handler (+0x44 = graphics+0x158, set by slot 6) in EDI.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CMaskedSpriteType::LoadKey(CMaskedSpriteType* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys of a `maskedShieldType`**, three cases, each through the string reader 0x67AFB0: token 0x25 `textureFile1` (the overlay) to +0x1C0, token 0x26 `textureFile2` (the mask) to +0x1A4, token 0x59 `effectFile` to **+0x1F4** - its own string, not CSpriteType's +0x5C. **Every other key goes to CSpriteType::LoadKey (0x6B7A00)**, so `allwaystransparent`, `transparencecheck`, `clicksound`, `noOfFrames` and `textureFile` are accepted too (core.gfx's GFX_minishield_war and eu3dialog.gfx's two dialog shields give `allwaystransparent`). `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Revised: the entry named the three keys and nothing else - not where each lands nor that the default forwards. Listing 0x84C030..0x84C08F: sub eax,0x25 / dec / sub 0x33 dispatch; +0x1C0 for 0x25, +0x1A4 for 0x26, +0x1F4 for 0x59, default `push edx; push eax; call 0xAB7A00`. Token names from ghidra/saveTokens.json (37 textureFile1, 38 textureFile2, 89 effectFile). Wrong if saveTokens.json's numbering is off; it is the table every other LoadKey entry cites.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::LoadResources
addresses.comment: Slot 6. **Loads the two pictures and the effect and takes the effect's handles by name.** +0x44 = graphics +0x158 (the texture handler); the mask (+0x1A4) through the handler (VA 0xA60F30, flag 1) into +0x210, the overlay (+0x1C0) into +0x214; each picture's own width and height (handler entry +0x24/+0x28 - the file's size, the texture being padded to a power of two) into +0x1DC/+0x1E0 (mask) and +0x1E4/+0x1E8 (overlay), 0 for an index of 10000 or more. **The effect: FxHandler_Register(graphics +0x6BCFC, path +0x1F4, key +0x1F4, device)** into +0x218 - the effectFile string is both path and key, so every masked sprite naming one file shares one ID3DXEffect. A plain quad of four (position, uv, white) vertices the mask's size, built by VA 0xA74470, into +0x220 - no draw read uses it. The effect pointer (the handler's list +0x6BD00, index - 1) into +0x21C, then GetParameterByName(NULL, ...) for `tex0` +0x224, `tex1` +0x228, `FlagCoords` +0x234, `WorldViewProjectionMatrix` +0x22C, and GetTechniqueByName for `tec0` +0x230, `over` +0x238, `down` +0x23C, `disable` +0x240. The argument is not read. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84C0A0..0x84C4D1 and the decompilation of a copy of the project: the eight strings are pushed at 0x84C3BA..0x84C47C into ID3DXEffect slots 9 (0x24, GetParameterByName) and 13 (0x34, GetTechniqueByName); 0xA61DD0 is FxHandler_Register (recorded) with +0x1F4 pushed twice. Wrong if slot 9/13 are not those methods - they are the ID3DXBaseEffect layout, and the same strings feed the same slots in the map's recorded reloads.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::ContainsPoint
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CMaskedSpriteType::ContainsPoint(CMaskedSpriteType* this, short* point, short* origin, float scale)
addresses.comment: Slot 16: whether `point` is inside the overlay's rectangle at `origin` - origin.x < point.x < origin.x + overlay width (+0x1E4) and the same for y with +0x1E8, **strict at both ends** (CSpriteType's own slot 16, VA 0xAB8270, is inclusive at the near end and scales the frame by `scale`); `scale` is not read here. The point's halves are read unsigned, the origin's signed. `ret 0xC`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84C4E0..0x84C527: movzx point, movsx origin, `cmp origin,point; jge` and `cmp origin+size,point; jle` for x then y, `mov al,1`/`xor al,al`, ret 0xC. Compared with 0xAB8270, which reads `[ebp+0x10]` as a float and `jg`s instead.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::IsTransparentAt
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CMaskedSpriteType::IsTransparentAt(CMaskedSpriteType* this, short* point, unsigned short frame)
addresses.comment: Slot 18, CSpriteType::IsTransparentAt (0x6B80E0) for a shield: true (see-through) where `allwaystransparent` (+0x178) is set. **`transparencecheck` is not asked**: the pixels are always tested. The point is moved by the mask's offset in the overlay (+0x1EC, +0x1F0 - each coordinate at or below the offset becomes 0) and is see-through where it is then past the mask's **width** in x or in y (+0x1DC both times - the height is not used, kept as read); else solid where the mask's alpha there is not nought (a DXT3 nibble, or byte 3 of a four-byte pixel); else the overlay is fetched by name (VA 0xA61300 on +0x1C0) and the point, unmoved, is solid where its alpha is not nought, see-through where it is. `frame` is not read. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84C530..0x84C79D: `cmp byte [ebx+0x178],0; jne return 1`; no read of +0x170 anywhere in the body; `mov ebx,[ebx+0x1dc]` compared with x at 0x84C5D7 and with y at 0x84C5E2; LockRect (texture slot 19) and GetLevelDesc (slot 17) on the +0x210 texture, then on 0xA61300's answer; `cmp ...,0x33545844` ('DXT3') both times. Wrong if 0xA61300 is not a lookup by name - it is handed the handler and the +0x1C0 string and its answer is locked like a texture.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag(CMaskedSpriteType* type, CGraphics* graphics, float* world, void* flagTexture, float* flagCoords, int state)
addresses.comment: **Draws the flag through the masked sprite's effect.** effect = the handler's list (+0x6BD00)[+0x218 - 1], kept at +0x21C. **Technique by `state`: 2 `down` (+0x23C), 3 `over` (+0x238), 4 `disable` (+0x240), anything else `tec0` (+0x230).** `WorldViewProjectionMatrix` = world (16 floats, the object's +0x94) x identity x **D3DXMatrixOrthoRH(screen width +0x6B9BC, screen height +0x6B9C0, 0, 1)**; `tex0` = flagTexture; `tex1` = the mask (+0x210 through the texture table, graphics +0x15C + 0x2C x index); +0x1EC = (int)((overlay width - mask width) x 0.5), +0x1F0 likewise for the height; `FlagCoords` = the four floats at flagCoords. Where world's float at +0x3C differs from +0x110 (-1.0 after slot 29), +0x110 takes it and slot 27 rebuilds the quad. Then Begin(&passes, 0), BeginPass(0), CommitChanges, VertexBuffer_Draw of the quad at +0xEC (FVF 0x202, a triangle fan), EndPass, End. Begin with flags 0 saves and restores the device state. One caller, CShieldObject::Render (VA 0x87EAA2). `ret 0x18`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84C7A0..0x84CAD4, one `ret 0x18`; the state switch at 0x84C7DB (sub 2 / dec / dec); the imports at IAT 0xD2B408 and 0xD2B438 resolve by name to D3DXMatrixOrthoRH and D3DXMatrixMultiply; ID3DXEffect slots 0xE8 SetTechnique, 0x98 SetMatrix, 0xD0 SetTexture, 0x88 SetVector, 0xFC..0x10C Begin/BeginPass/CommitChanges/EndPass/End; 0xAD4C30 is VertexBuffer_Draw (recorded). findRefs --callers: one call, from 0x87EAA2. Wrong if the state values mean something else - CShieldObject::UpdateStateName (0x706050) maps the same 2/3/4 to the strings down/over/disable.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::CreateInstance
addresses.comment: Slot 23: operator new(0x1AC) and CShieldObject::CShieldObject with this type in ECX, the graphics (+0x1A0), the flag atlas (+0x244) and the address of `arg`; null where the allocation fails. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84CAE0..0x84CB52: push 0x1AC; call 0xB9602F; pushes [esi+0x244], [esi+0x1a0], lea [ebp+8]; mov ecx, esi; call 0x87E760. The object's vftable written there is CShieldObject's (RTTI, 0x15E3A8C).

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::GetSize
addresses.comment: Slot 17: out = the overlay's width and height (+0x1E4, +0x1E8) - **the size of the sprite is textureFile1's**, where CSpriteType's slot 17 (VA 0xAB80C0) answers +0xA4/+0xA8. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84CB60..0x84CB78, eight instructions; CSpriteType's 0xAB80C0 is the same shape on +0xA4/+0xA8.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::CreateQuadBuffer
addresses.comment: Slot 29: +0x110 = -1.0 (the float at VA 0x170AC0C), releases the quad MeshBuffer at +0xEC, clears it, primitive kind (+0x10C) 2 - a triangle fan - not managed, and **VertexBuffer_Create(+0xEC, device, 4 vertices, stride 0x1C, FVF 0x202 = XYZ|TEX2, not dynamic)**: position and two texture coordinates a vertex. CSpriteType's own slot 29 (VA 0xAB7750) makes a 0x14-stride XYZ|TEX1 strip. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84CB80..0x84CC07: `mov dword [edi+0x10c], 2`, `push 0; push 0x202; push 0x1c; push 4; push device; push esi; call 0xAD4510` (VertexBuffer_Create, recorded). The float at 0x170AC0C reads 0xBF800000 = -1.0.

addresses.name: CMaskedSpriteType::BuildQuad
addresses.comment: Slot 27: **fills the four vertices of the masked flag**, calling slot 29 first where the buffer has no vertices (+0xF8). With W, H the mask's size (+0x1DC, +0x1E0), FW, FH the overlay's (+0x1E4, +0x1E8), ox = (FW - W) x 0.5, oy = (FH - H) x 0.5, R the turn by the rotation +0xA0 (x' = cos x - sin y, y' = sin x + cos y; _CIcos 0xC0BCC0, _CIsin 0xC0BB90), w2 = W/2 and h2 = H/2 in whole numbers and P(n) the least power of two not below n: v0 = R(ox - w2, oy - h2) + (w2, h2), uv (0,1), mask uv (0, H/P(H)); v1 = R(ox - W/2, oy + H/2) + (W/2, H/2), (0,0), (0,0); v2 = R(ox + W/2, oy + H/2) + (W/2, H/2), (1,0), (W/P(W), 0); v3 = R(ox + w2, oy - h2) + (W/2, H/2), (1,1), (W/P(W), H/P(H)); z = 1.0 for all. y runs up. The lock asks D3DLOCK_DISCARD only for a dynamic buffer. Bare `ret` at 0x84D394. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x84CC10..0x84D394 and the decompilation: the two power-of-two loops at 0x84CCC0/0x84CD05, the `sar eax,1` halves against the `mulsd [0x160A308]` (0.5) halves vertex by vertex, the stores to the locked buffer at stride 0x1C (floats 3-6, 10-13, 17-20, 24-27 the texture coordinates), Unlock (slot 12). 0xC0BCC0 and 0xC0BB90 reach `fcos` and `fsin`. Wrong if +0xA0 is not the rotation - CShieldObject::Render writes its +0x14C there immediately before calling this slot.

addresses.name: CShieldObject::CShieldObject
addresses.signature: CShieldObject* __stdcall CShieldObject::CShieldObject(CShieldObject* this@stack:4, CGraphics* graphics@stack:8, void* flagAtlas@stack:0xC, void* arg@stack:0x10, CMaskedSpriteType* type@ECX) @EAX

addresses.evidence: Listing 0x87E760..0x87E82B: `mov edi, ecx`, `[esi+0x184] = edi`, `push 0x15C1E74 'SWE'; lea ecx,[esi+0x18c]; call 0x518480` (CCountryDataBase::GetTag, recorded), +0x1A0 = [ebp+0x10], +0x194/+0x198 from [edi+0x1e4]/[edi+0x1e8]; one caller, CMaskedSpriteType::CreateInstance.

addresses.name: CShieldObject::DeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 9 (this family's destructor slot; slot 0 is a getter): writes the vftable back, frees the string at +0x15C, calls the base destructor (VA 0xA5F190), frees the object where bit 0 of `flags` is set. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x87E6C0..0x87E716; vtable.py --holding: CShieldObject slot 9 only. Slot 0 (0xB06430) is `mov eax,[ecx+0x150]; add eax,0x17c; ret`.

addresses.name: CShieldObject::Render
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CShieldObject::Render(CShieldObject* this, CGraphics* graphics, void* device, int arg3, int arg4, unsigned short state, int arg6)
addresses.comment: Slot 10: **draws the shield - the flag through the effect, then the overlay over it.** Saves ZENABLE and ZWRITEENABLE and sets both 1, FOGVERTEXMODE 0, **SRCBLEND SRCALPHA (5), DESTBLEND INVSRCALPHA (6)**. The flag's cell: id = +0x190, 0 taken as 1; the atlas's cells (+0x14) are rows of {u, v} pairs, `columns` a row, and cell id - 1 gives (u, v); **FlagCoords = (columns +0x28, rows +0x24, u, v)** as floats and the texture the atlas's own (+0); **where +0x1A4 holds a picture, FlagCoords = (1, 1, 0, 0) and that picture instead**. Where the object's rotation +0x14C differs from the type's +0xA0 it is copied there and the type's slot 27 rebuilds the quad. Then CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag(type, graphics, this +0x94, texture, &FlagCoords, state). **Then the overlay**: four vertices R(+-FW/2, +-FH/2) + (FW/2, FH/2), z 1.0, uv (0, FH/P(FH)), (0,0), (FW/P(FW), 0), (FW/P(FW), FH/P(FH)) - FW, FH from +0x194/+0x198, R by +0x14C, halves times 0.5 - SetTexture(0, the type's +0x214 overlay), ALPHABLENDENABLE 1, SetFVF(0x102), DrawPrimitiveUP(TRIANGLEFAN, 2, stride 0x14), ALPHABLENDENABLE 0, and the two depth states put back. `state` picks the technique for the flag only; the overlay is drawn the same in every state. `ret 0x18`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x87E830..0x87F156 read whole: device slots 0xE8/0xE4 (Get/SetRenderState) with 7, 0xE, 0x8C, 0x13, 0x14, 0x1B; the cell arithmetic at 0x87E8F2..0x87E9CF (idiv by (end-begin)>>3, cvtdq2ps of [atlas+0x28] then [atlas+0x24]); the (1,1,0,0) branch at 0x87E9E9; slot 0x6C of the type at 0x87EA2F/0x87EA70; the call at 0x87EAA2; SetTexture 0x104, SetFVF 0x164 with 0x102, DrawPrimitiveUP 0x14C with (6, 2, 0x14). Wrong about the cell layout if the atlas's rows were not `columns` long - the atlas built from TFH's 101 flags (gfx/flags/flagfiles.tga) has 8 columns of 16 rows and 97 of 101 cells match their flag file at six sample points.

addresses.name: LoadFlags
addresses.comment: **Builds the flag atlas**: FlagTextureMap_Build(graphics +0x6BD6C, "gfx/flags", the country database (made if missing), graphics). Called once from LoadEverything at 0x6326B1 with ECX = the application's graphics ([edi+0x11C]), between the sound-effect stage and the `Loading Flags <` timer (eu3application.cpp:553). Extent 0x840BC0..0x840C66, bare `ret`. The graphics arrive in ECX and nothing is passed on the stack. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 5, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-startup.md.
addresses.evidence: Revised: the entry was `void __cdecl LoadFlags(void)` with the interior unread; it uses ECX (`mov esi, ecx` at 0x840BDF, `add esi, 0x6bd6c` at 0x840C39), so a no-argument __cdecl signature loses the graphics. Listing 0x840BC0..0x840C66 read whole; caller 0x6326A6 loads ECX from [edi+0x11C]. Name kept, so nothing that cites it moves.

addresses.name: FlagTextureMap_Build
addresses.signature: void __stdcall FlagTextureMap_Build(void* map, Hoi3CString* folder, CCountryDataBase* countries, CGraphics* graphics)
addresses.comment: **Makes the flag atlas every masked shield and `@TAG` in text draw from** (log lines name flagtexturemap.cpp; the name is ours). `map` is CGraphics +0x6BD6C. One flag file a country: `<TAG>.tga` for every country of the database whose tag starts with a letter, in database order. N flags: s = (int)sqrt(N); where s is a power of two, rows = s and columns = s, columns = the next power of two above s where s x s < N; otherwise rows = the least power of two not below s and columns = the least power of two not below ceil(N / rows). map +0x24 = rows, +0x28 = columns. The texture is P(93 x columns) by P(64 x rows) (+0x2C = 93 and +0x30 = 64 from CEU3Graphics::CEU3Graphics), so a cell is texture width / columns by texture height / rows; each flag is drawn whole into its cell; the cell of country id k is k - 1, row-major from the top, and map +0x14 holds each row's {u = column / columns, v = row / rows}. A render target cleared to white (0xFFFFFFFF) holds the drawing, which is copied into an A8R8G8B8 texture (+0). The result is cached as gfx/flags/flagfiles.tga, with flagfiles.txt listing `PowerOf2` and every flag file in order; logs `Missing flag for <TAG>` and `Failed to load flag texture`. When the cache is used rather than rebuilt (the test 0x8417E0) was not read. Extent 0x8427C0..0x844A55, `ret 0x10`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read in parts, by the decompilation and the listing: the tag loop and `.tga`, the sqrt and power-of-two branches storing +0x28/+0x24 at 0x843C5F/0x843C62, the texture size from +0x2C x columns and +0x30 x rows at 0x843CB5..0x843CF6, the cell origins column/columns and row/rows at 0x844431..0x84447A, the strings flagfiles.txt/.tga, PowerOf2 in the cache, Clear(..., 0xFFFFFFFF). Checked against the install's gfx/flags/flagfiles.tga: 1024 x 1024, 101 flags in 8 columns and 16 rows of 128 x 64, unused cells white, 97 of 101 cells matching their flag at six sample points. Inferred because the per-flag load parameters, the cache test and the drawing pass were not read through.

structs.name: CMaskedSpriteType
structs.comment: A `maskedShieldType` of the .gfx files: a country's flag drawn through a mask (textureFile2) with an overlay (textureFile1) over it, through effectFile. Its drawn object is a CShieldObject. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md.
structs.evidence: operator new(0x250) at VA 0x8409CB immediately before the constructor; RTTI gives CMaskedSpriteType : CSpriteType at offset 0 and the table 0x15E1D44 (rva 0x11E1D44), the address the constructor writes.

structs.name: CShieldObject
structs.comment: The object a CMaskedSpriteType makes for each element that shows it (slot 23): which country's flag, or a picture of its own, and the draw. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-maskedflag.md.
structs.evidence: operator new(0x1AC) in CMaskedSpriteType::CreateInstance before CShieldObject::CShieldObject; RTTI gives CShieldObject : CSprite at offset 0 and the table 0x15E3A8C, which the constructor writes.

struct_fields.name: graphics
struct_fields.comment: The graphics, from the constructor's ECX: device +0x64, texture handler +0x158, effect handler +0x6BCFC, screen size +0x6B9BC.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x84BE3B; every draw reads +0x64, +0x158/+0x15C, +0x6BCFC/+0x6BD00 through it.

struct_fields.name: mask_file
struct_fields.comment: `textureFile2`: the mask, whose alpha is the shield's shape. Loaded into +0x210.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey token 0x26 case at 0x84C068; LoadResources loads it into +0x210, which the draw hands to `tex1`.

struct_fields.name: overlay_file
struct_fields.comment: `textureFile1`: the overlay drawn over the flag (a frame, a shadow). Loaded into +0x214; its size is the sprite's.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey token 0x25 case at 0x84C07D; CShieldObject::Render draws +0x214 after the flag.

struct_fields.name: mask_width
struct_fields.comment: The mask file's own width (the texture handler's entry +0x24), not the padded texture's.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadResources 0x84C125; BuildQuad divides it by its next power of two for the mask's texture coordinate.

struct_fields.name: mask_height
struct_fields.comment: The mask file's own height.

struct_fields.name: overlay_width
struct_fields.comment: The overlay file's own width: the sprite's width (slot 17) and the box the mask is centred in.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadResources 0x84C155; GetSize, ContainsPoint and the CShieldObject constructor read it.

struct_fields.name: overlay_height
struct_fields.comment: The overlay file's own height.

struct_fields.name: mask_offset_x
struct_fields.comment: (int)((overlay width - mask width) x 0.5), written by every flag draw and by nothing else; IsTransparentAt moves a point by it. The quad itself is built from the unrounded half.

struct_fields.name: mask_offset_y
struct_fields.comment: (int)((overlay height - mask height) x 0.5), as +0x1EC.

struct_fields.name: masked_effect_file
struct_fields.comment: `effectFile`, this class's own (CSpriteType's +0x5C is left empty): the path handed to FxHandler_Register and also its key.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey token 0x59 case at 0x84C053; LoadResources pushes +0x1F4 twice into 0xA61DD0.

struct_fields.name: mask_texture
struct_fields.comment: The mask's index in the texture handler (-1 none); its texture is graphics +0x15C + 0x2C x index. `tex1`.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadResources 0x84C0EA; CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag 0x84C943..0x84C980 (SetTexture on the tex1 handle).

struct_fields.name: overlay_texture
struct_fields.comment: The overlay's index in the texture handler; drawn by CShieldObject::Render after the flag, fixed-function.

struct_fields.name: effect_index
struct_fields.comment: FxHandler_Register's answer: the effect is the handler's list (graphics +0x6BD00) at index - 1.

struct_fields.name: effect
struct_fields.comment: The ID3DXEffect, fetched again from the handler at every draw.

struct_fields.name: plain_quad
struct_fields.comment: A mesh of four (position, uv, white) vertices the mask's size, made by VA 0xA74470 in LoadResources and released in the destructor. No draw read here uses it.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadResources 0x84C39A; ~CMaskedSpriteType 0x84BF2B. Neither CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag nor CShieldObject::Render reads +0x220.

struct_fields.name: handle_tex0
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of the effect's `tex0`: the flag (the atlas, or the shield's own picture).

struct_fields.name: handle_tex1
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of `tex1`: the mask.

struct_fields.name: handle_world_view_projection
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of `WorldViewProjectionMatrix`: the object's matrix x D3DXMatrixOrthoRH(screen width, screen height, 0, 1).

struct_fields.name: technique_tec0
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of the technique `tec0`, used for every state but 2, 3 and 4.

struct_fields.name: handle_flag_coords
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of `FlagCoords`: (columns, rows, cell u, cell v) of the flag atlas, or (1, 1, 0, 0) for a picture of the shield's own.

struct_fields.name: technique_over
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of `over`, state 3.

struct_fields.name: technique_down
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of `down`, state 2.

struct_fields.name: technique_disable
struct_fields.comment: D3DXHANDLE of `disable`, state 4.

struct_fields.name: flag_atlas
struct_fields.comment: The flag atlas, &CGraphics +0x6BD6C, from the constructor; handed to every CShieldObject it makes.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x84BEB4 from the factory's `lea ecx,[edi+0x6bd6c]`; CreateInstance pushes it.

struct_fields.name: rotation
struct_fields.comment: The rotation in radians the type's shared quad (+0xEC) was last built at. CShieldObject::Render copies its object's +0x14C here and calls slot 27 where they differ; CMaskedSpriteType::BuildQuad turns each corner by it; CSpriteType's own slot 27 tests it at VA 0xAB882B. Read on the masked type; that it means the same on every sprite type is likely, not read.
struct_fields.evidence: CShieldObject::Render 0x87EA32/0x87EA73 (store then slot 0x6C); BuildQuad's fld [edi+0xa0] into _CIcos/_CIsin at 0x84CDA4 and three more.

struct_fields.name: quad
struct_fields.comment: The type's one quad, shared by every object drawn with it: a 0x24-byte MeshBuffer made by slot 29 (CSpriteType: 4 vertices, stride 0x14, XYZ|TEX1, a strip; CMaskedSpriteType: stride 0x1C, XYZ|TEX2, a fan) and filled by slot 27.
struct_fields.evidence: CMaskedSpriteType::CreateQuadBuffer and CSpriteType's slot 29 (VA 0xAB775D) both `lea esi,[edi+0xec]` and call VertexBuffer_Create on it; CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag draws it with VertexBuffer_Draw (eax = +0xEC at 0x84CA9F).

struct_fields.name: quad_scale
struct_fields.comment: Set to -1.0 when the quad buffer is made (slot 29), so the next draw rebuilds it; the masked draw compares it with the object's matrix float at +0x3C and rebuilds where they differ. CSpriteType's own quad builder multiplies by it (VA 0xAB85C1), hence the name; the masked builder does not read it.
struct_fields.evidence: Slot 29 stores [0x170AC0C] = -1.0 at 0x84CB93 and 0xAB7763; CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag 0x84CA2B..0x84CA52; CSpriteType slot 27 0xAB85C1..0xAB8600 (fmul).

struct_fields.name: type
struct_fields.comment: The masked sprite type it is drawn with (slot 91 answers it).
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x87E7A0 from ECX; Render passes it to CMaskedSpriteType_DrawFlag.

struct_fields.name: graphics
struct_fields.comment: The graphics; Render takes the device's render states through +0x64.

struct_fields.name: country
struct_fields.comment: Whose flag: tag and id. SWE's from the constructor, until SetCountry. Render picks the atlas cell by the id at +0x190, 0 taken as 1.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x87E7E4 (GetTag "SWE" into +0x18C); SetCountry writes +0x18C/+0x190; Render reads +0x190 at 0x87E8F2.

struct_fields.name: overlay_width
struct_fields.comment: Copied from the type's +0x1E4: the overlay quad's width.

struct_fields.name: overlay_height
struct_fields.comment: Copied from the type's +0x1E8.

struct_fields.name: flag_atlas
struct_fields.comment: The flag atlas (&CGraphics +0x6BD6C): +0 its texture, +0x14 its rows of {u, v} cells, +0x24 rows, +0x28 columns.

struct_fields.name: picture
struct_fields.comment: An IDirect3DTexture9 set by SetTexture (slot 84) and cleared by SetCountry: where set, it is drawn whole through the mask in place of the flag.

struct_fields.name: country_id
struct_fields.comment: The id last given to SetCountry; slot 85 answers it.

struct_fields.name: flag_atlas_texture
struct_fields.comment: The flag atlas's texture (IDirect3DTexture9), the first member of the flag texture map that starts here and that FlagTextureMap_Build fills; every masked shield's `tex0` unless it has a picture of its own, and the `@TAG` icon's texture.
struct_fields.evidence: CShieldObject::Render hands *(map) to the draw as the texture (0x87EA88); CEU3Graphics::CEU3Graphics zeroes it (0x8406B9); LoadFlags passes &graphics+0x6BD6C to the builder.

struct_fields.name: flag_atlas_cells
struct_fields.comment: The flag atlas's rows: 16-byte records whose first two dwords are the begin and end of that row's 8-byte {float u, float v} cells, `columns` a row.
struct_fields.evidence: Map +0x14: CShieldObject::Render 0x87E907..0x87E933 and CEU3BitmapFont::DrawFlagIcon index it the same way; the builder sizes each row with +0x28 entries (0x843C89).

struct_fields.name: flag_atlas_cells_end
struct_fields.comment: End of the rows at +0x6BD80: (end - begin) / 16 is the number of rows.
struct_fields.evidence: FlagTextureMap_Build 0x843C6A..0x843CA8 (`sar edx, 4` against the row counter).

struct_fields.name: flag_atlas_rows
struct_fields.comment: Rows of the flag atlas: `FlagCoords.y`. 16 for Their Finest Hour's 101 flags.

struct_fields.name: flag_atlas_columns
struct_fields.comment: Columns of the flag atlas: `FlagCoords.x`. 8 for Their Finest Hour's 101 flags.

struct_fields.name: flag_cell_width
struct_fields.comment: 93, set by CEU3Graphics::CEU3Graphics: the atlas's width is the least power of two not below 93 x columns.

struct_fields.name: flag_cell_height
struct_fields.comment: 64, set by CEU3Graphics::CEU3Graphics: the atlas's height is the least power of two not below 64 x rows.
